title: Norway to propose temporary ban on AI glasses in some public places
key_facts: Norway's government said on Monday 5 Oct 2026 it plans to propose a temporary ban on AI glasses in selected places.
Concern: people could be photographed, filmed or audio-recorded without knowing.
Could cover parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres, public events, schools, playgrounds, youth clubs, doctors' offices, swimming pools and gyms with changing rooms.
Not a total ban; private use and use where others are not at risk of being filmed would stay allowed.
Government will examine which devices are covered, including glasses with camera and audio or AI, or other body-worn technology.
A bill will go to parliament as soon as possible and an expert group will advise on permanent rules.
quote_evidence: I am worried that new, powerful technology is being introduced where people risk being photographed, filmed or audio-recorded without knowing it,
The proposal mirrors a broader global backlash against smart glasses equipped with cameras over privacy concerns
why_it_matters_hint: A government move against camera glasses on privacy grounds.
